steps: Write TS-13-1 (--effort registered with DeclareEnum listing seven values), TS-13-2 (Common has Effort, no Variant), TS-13-5 (case-insensitive matching stored as lower-case), TS-13-6 (invalid --effort exits 2 listing accepted values), TS-13-7 (invalid $AF_MODEL_EFFORT exits 2 naming the variable), and TS-13-17 (--variant no longer registered) and confirm they fail.

Implement case-insensitive matching: use a custom flag.Value type (or normalize in a ValidEffort method) that lowercases the input and checks membership in the accepted set. An invalid value returns an error listing the accepted values.

steps: Write TS-13-3 (effort precedence table test), TS-13-4 (--effort applies to catalog id), TS-13-8 (ClampThinkingLevel called and clamped level used), TS-13-9 (effort_clamped warning recorded), TS-13-10 (ok==false with explicit effort fails), and TS-13-11 (WarnEffortClamped maps to preflight) and confirm they fail.

If ok==false and the effort was explicit (from flag or env), return a usage error naming the model. Update ResolveModelNamed's signature or add a Run parameter so it can record warnings. If ResolveModelNamed currently has no access to Run, thread it through or return warnings alongside the ModelChoice for the caller to record.
Run go test ./internal/toolio/... ./internal/agentrun/... -count=1 and confirm all tests pass.

tasks.title: Add --repair-model-effort to impl and implement repair effort precedence
steps: Write TS-13-12 (--repair-model-effort registered on impl, in toolFlags), TS-13-13 (repair effort precedence table test), TS-13-14 (--repair-model-effort alone implies --repair), TS-13-15 (repair clamping warning names repair phase), and TS-13-16 (no env var fallback for --repair-model-effort) and confirm they fail.

In internal/toolio/toolflags.go, add "repair-model-effort" to toolFlags["impl"].
In cmd/impl/main.go's PreCheck, add logic: if f.repairModelEffort != "" { f.repair = true } (--repair-model-effort implies --repair).

Update resolveRepairRunner (or add a new function) to implement the repair effort precedence: (1) --repair-model-effort, (2) if --repair-model is given: that model's tier effort (via ResolveModelNamed), otherwise ThinkingUnset, (3) if --repair-model is not given: the run's effective effort. The run's --effort and $AF_MODEL_EFFORT do not carry over to a separately named repair model.
Ensure the repair model's effort goes through the same ClampThinkingLevel check and records an effort_clamped warning whose message names the repair phase.
Run go test ./cmd/impl/... -count=1 and confirm all tests pass.
